`cryptcheck` currently only compares file differences.  I think it would be useful for it to also report directory differences, that is, if a directory exists on one side but not the other.

It seems logical that any detectable differences should be reported by `cryptcheck`, which would include directory checks.

body:
That's because you are mixing crypt and non crypt.

Fix your remotes so they don't mix..

@animosity22 that is beside the point.  `sync` should make the destination identical to the source, and should delete any files and directories that do not exist on the source, whether they are crypted or not.  In this case, sync is not doing that.

And as an aside, these leftover files were at some point created by `rclone`, as this remote has never been touched as non-crypt.  I haven't been able to track down why yet, but when I do I'll be filing a bug on that as well.  I think it has something to do with exceeding the storable cryptable filename length.

If the file name is too long, you get a message stating such as that's an easy one to produce.

The use case here is at some point, you probably accidentally copied from a non crypt location to a crypt location by mistake.

@animosity22 that is a presumption without any evidence on your part, and I'm stating that that's not the case.  I merely offered the info to dispel your presumption, even though it is off topic to this bug report.

Isn't yours a presumption too as there's no evidence? :)

I'm just sharing what I've seen over reading tons of posts, debug logs, etc. The only time I've seen that use case is by an accidental copy from a non crypted remote to a crypt location in a remote.

That's my "theory" which has no malice, ill will, bad intent or anything else.

Could there be a bug? Sure. Could I be incorrect? Sure. I'm sharing my thoughts based on my experience.

This is not an enhancement, it is a bug.  Please mark it as so, since it clearly a violation of the stated operation of `sync`.  There is an exception made in the documentation for duplicate objects, but that is not the case here (directory vs files with errors).

It's really an enhancement as garbage in there isn't a bug but a flow issue or a bug somewhere else per your message if something else caused it but the label really doesn't matter than much imo so I changed it.

issue.title: operations: --no-block-rmdir for disposable files blocking removal of otherwise empty directory

repository.name: rclone
repository.description: "rsync for cloud storage" - Google Drive, S3, Dropbox, Backblaze B2, One Drive, Swift, Hubic, Wasabi, Google Cloud Storage, Azure Blob, Azure Files, Yandex Files

issue.body:
#### What is the purpose of this change?

Before this change, rclone commands that remove empty dirs (including `rmdir`, `rmdirs`, `sync`, and `bisync`) would silently fail to remove dirs if those dirs contained files that were excluded by filters. This can pose a problem for some automatically created system files, such as `.DS_Store` on macOS, which users often prefer to exclude from syncs -- including them makes for noisy logs, but excluding them can make it impossible to remove otherwise empty directories.

After this change, a new `--no-block-rmdir` flag allows specifying a comma-separated list of such files which rclone should consider "disposable" if they block removal of otherwise empty directories. When set, if rclone fails to remove a directory, it will check the contents of the directory (ignoring any filters.) If the directory contains ONLY files on the disposable list, rclone will delete the files and then remove the directory.

#### Was the change discussed in an issue or in the forum before?

See partially-related #6437

issue.body:
#### What is the purpose of this change?

Before this change, undecryptable file names would be skipped very quietly (there was a log warning, but only at `DEBUG` level), failing to alert users of a potentially serious issue that needs attention.

After this change, the log level is raised to `NOTICE` by default and a new `--crypt-strict-names` flag allows raising an error, for users who may prefer not to proceed if such an issue is detected.
